presentation.title: Fake Charity / Disaster Donation Scam
presentation.summary: After fictional flooding in Cedar Valley County, an emotional donation appeal uses a vague charity identity, a matching-gift deadline, social proof, caller pressure, and unusual payment requests.
presentation.practiceGoal: Donate through a verified charity selected independently rather than through an emotional pressure link, unexpected caller, or unusual payment instruction.

warningSigns.sign: Emotional disaster images and supporter comments were treated as proof of an organization.
The appeal used Donate Now urgency and a one-hour matching-gift countdown.
The charity name was vague, and the exact organization could not be independently verified.
A similarly named organization was not the same charity.
The supplied registration number, incomplete address, and recently created-looking domain did not match an independent record.
The donation link came from the same unexpected post that made the claims.
The form requested excessive personal information, preselected recurring giving, and added processing costs.
The payment-app recipient was a person rather than the charity.
Wire transfer, cryptocurrency, gift cards, and person-to-person payments were major warning signs.
The caller's callback number, employee ID, and mailed information were not independent proof.
Guilt and the phrase "Every minute you wait, families suffer" shortened decision-making time.
A small donation and an initial payment led to additional requests.

finalReview.safestAction: Choose the charity independently, verify the exact organization and website, and donate only through contact information or a donation page you locate yourself.

realWorldActions.action: If the appeal was shared, remove or correct it, notify people who may have seen it, and report the original post.
If contact information was entered, stop contact, preserve evidence, review privacy settings, and expect targeted follow-up messages.
If card details were entered, contact the card issuer through a trusted number, review transactions and recurring payments, and follow its security instructions.
If money was sent, contact the bank, card issuer, payment provider, or gift-card issuer immediately through independently located information and ask what actions may still be available.
Preserve posts, website details, messages, caller information, receipts, and transaction records, and report the appeal through legitimate channels.
Tell someone trusted and be cautious of anyone promising guaranteed recovery for an upfront fee.

artifact.heading: Simulated CommunityPost disaster appeal
artifact.message: National Relief Support Fund posts: "Local families lost everything. Donate in the next hour to double your impact. A private sponsor will match every gift made through this emergency link." A flood photograph, a 59-minute visual countdown, comments saying "Donated!" and "Thank you for helping!", and a large Donate Now button surround the appeal. No operator, complete address, or independently verifiable record is shown.

requestedInformation.item: Donation through the supplied emergency link
Immediate action before the fictional match expires
Sharing the appeal with friends and family

artifact.transcript: A clearly simulated CommunityPost page follows severe flooding in fictional Cedar Valley County. A post from the fictional National Relief Support Fund says, "Local families lost everything. Donate in the next hour to double your impact." It claims a private sponsor will match every gift through the supplied emergency link. A disaster photograph, a visual countdown that does not control the learner, supportive comments, and a Donate Now button create urgency and social proof. The post does not identify who operates the charity, provide a complete address, or offer independently verifiable details.

scene.question: What would you do before donating or sharing?
scene.description: The desire to help is reasonable. Decide how to verify that help will reach the intended people.

warningSigns.sign: Emotional imagery and supporter comments are being used as proof.
A one-hour match discourages careful checking.
The charity identity and supplied link have not been independently verified.

choice.title: Search for the exact charity independently
choice.subtitle: Do not use the post's link; look for the exact organization, registration, address, and website through separate sources.

feedback.heading: Compassion leaves room for verification
feedback.consequence: No information or money is shared while the exact organization is checked.
feedback.explanation: Emotional images may be real, old, unrelated, copied, or taken from legitimate coverage. Comments and share counts do not verify who receives the money.

warningSigns.sign: The matching deadline attempts to replace verification with urgency.

choice.title: Open the supplied donation link
choice.subtitle: Visit the page from the unexpected post to learn more.

feedback.heading: The poster still controls the evidence
feedback.consequence: The supplied link opens a polished donation site, but the source has not become independent.
feedback.explanation: Looking is not the same as paying, yet a professional page can reinforce claims made by the same unverified organization.

warningSigns.sign: The link and every claim behind it came from the appeal.

choice.title: Share the appeal without donating
choice.subtitle: Help the post reach friends while the matching countdown continues.

feedback.heading: Sharing can transfer trust to an unverified appeal
feedback.consequence: Friends and relatives begin seeing the appeal as something recommended by a person they know.
feedback.explanation: Sharing does not cost money immediately, but it can spread an unverified link to people who trust you.

warningSigns.sign: Borrowed trust can make a false appeal look safer.

artifact.heading: Simulated sharing notifications

requestedInformation.item: Keep the original donation link visible

artifact.transcript: A simulated CommunityPost notification page shows that the learner's shared disaster appeal reached friends and relatives. Two people reshared it, and one says a donation was made because the learner posted it. The same unverified link and visual matching countdown remain visible. A trusted person's share may look like verification even when that person was also relying on the original post.

scene.question: What would you do with the shared post now?
scene.description: Correcting an unverified post is responsible, not embarrassing.

warningSigns.sign: People are treating a trusted person's share as evidence.
Social proof is growing without independent verification.

choice.title: Remove or correct the shared post
choice.subtitle: Warn people who saw it, report the original appeal, and verify any future charity independently.

feedback.heading: You interrupted the spread of the appeal
feedback.consequence: The unverified link is removed or clearly corrected before more people rely on it.
feedback.explanation: Taking responsibility for a correction protects the same community you wanted to help.

warningSigns.sign: The reshares showed how quickly borrowed trust can spread.

choice.title: Add "I have not verified this yet" and investigate
choice.subtitle: Leave the link visible while searching for the exact organization separately.

feedback.heading: The warning helps, but the link remains available
feedback.consequence: Verification begins, although some readers may still act on the visible appeal.
feedback.explanation: A correction or removal is stronger than a caveat when an unverified payment link is already spreading.

warningSigns.sign: People may notice the emotional appeal more than the added warning.

choice.title: Encourage everyone to donate before the match ends
choice.subtitle: Use the countdown and supporter comments to urge faster action.

feedback.heading: Urgency spreads with the unverified link
feedback.consequence: More people may trust the appeal because the recommendation now comes from someone they know.
feedback.explanation: Manufactured social proof can include well-meaning people who have not checked the exact organization.

warningSigns.sign: The deadline is driving promotion before verification.

artifact.heading: Simulated National Relief Support Fund website
artifact.message: A polished fictional page repeats the flood photographs and 100-percent-to-victims claim. It shows a registration badge, broad testimonials, suggested donation buttons, and a private-donor countdown. The page names no board members, offers no detailed finances, gives only "Cedar Valley area" as an address, and uses a recently created-looking domain.

requestedInformation.item: Choose a suggested donation amount
Trust the displayed registration badge
Donate before the visual match expires

artifact.transcript: A simulated donation website for the fictional National Relief Support Fund displays disaster photographs, testimonials, a visual countdown, suggested amounts, and a claim that one hundred percent of donations go directly to victims. It shows fictional registration number NRSF-000-EXAMPLE but no verifiable leadership, detailed finances, or complete address. The domain looks recently created. The page is polished, but all evidence is supplied by the same unverified organization.

scene.description: A professional design and lock symbol do not verify the organization behind a site.

Leadership, finances, address, and registration cannot be confirmed on the page.

feedback.heading: A separate source can test the site's claims
feedback.consequence: The supplied page no longer controls where verification happens.
feedback.explanation: The exact organization and exact website must match independent records; a similar name is not enough.

warningSigns.sign: The site could not supply independently confirmable details.

choice.title: Trust the photos, testimonials, and registration badge
choice.subtitle: Continue because the page looks professional and supporters sound genuine.

feedback.heading: Polished claims are still self-supplied claims
feedback.consequence: The simulated donation form opens before the exact charity is verified.

choice.title: Make a small donation as a test

artifact.heading: Simulated independent charity-verification search
artifact.message: No exact registered organization is found for National Relief Support Fund. Fictional registration number NRSF-000-EXAMPLE has no matching record, the supplied address is incomplete, and a similarly named group is a different organization. An independently located option, Cedar Valley Community Recovery Alliance, has its own matching registration, complete address, leadership information, and separate website.

requestedInformation.item: Compare the exact organization name
Compare the exact website, registration, address, and contact information
Choose whether and where to donate

artifact.transcript: A clearly labeled simulated independent verification screen searches the exact name National Relief Support Fund. No exact registered organization appears. The fictional registration number from the donation page returns no match, and the supplied Cedar Valley area address is incomplete and unrelated to a registered office. A similarly named organization is not the same charity. The fictional Cedar Valley Community Recovery Alliance appears through an independently located record with different contact information, its own website, a complete address, leadership information, and a matching fictional registration. The learner can donate safely to disaster relief without using the original appeal.

warningSigns.sign: No exact record matches National Relief Support Fund.
The displayed registration number and address do not match an independent record.
A similar name could be mistaken for the original organization.

choice.subtitle: Use the Cedar Valley Community Recovery Alliance website found through the independent record.

feedback.heading: You preserved the goal of helping

feedback.explanation: Verification protects both the donor and the people the donor wants to help.

choice.title: Report the appeal and donate later

feedback.heading: Waiting does not reduce compassion

warningSigns.sign: The original appeal could not survive an exact independent check.

choice.title: Confirm the exact registration mismatch and stop

feedback.heading: The exact record does not match

warningSigns.sign: The supplied registration number produces no matching record.

choice.title: Assume the similar name proves the original site
choice.subtitle: Return to National Relief Support Fund because another relief group has a related-sounding name.

feedback.heading: Similar names are different organizations
feedback.consequence: The unverified site's donation form opens despite the failed exact match.

warningSigns.sign: The record found belongs to a different organization.

choice.title: Return because verification takes too long

feedback.heading: The countdown replaces evidence with pressure
feedback.consequence: The donation form opens even though the exact organization was not found.

artifact.heading: Simulated, nonfunctional donation form
artifact.message: The page requests full name, email, phone, home address, date of birth, donation amount, card details, and future fundraising permission. "Make this a monthly gift" is selected by default, an extra processing amount is added, cancellation details are unclear, and the matching countdown remains visible.

requestedInformation.item: Full contact information and unnecessary date of birth
Card number, expiration date, and security code

artifact.transcript: A clearly simulated and nonfunctional donation form requests the learner's full name, email, phone number, home address, date of birth, donation amount, card information, and permission for future fundraising contacts. A monthly recurring gift is selected by default, an extra processing amount is added, and refund or cancellation information is unclear. A visual countdown continues, but it does not limit learner response time. No information can actually be submitted.

scene.question: What would you do at the donation form?
scene.description: Distinguish contact-information exposure, card exposure, payment, and recurring-payment risk.

warningSigns.sign: The form requests more identifying information than the donation requires.
A recurring gift and extra cost are selected or added by default.
A lock symbol and familiar form design do not verify the charity.

choice.title: Close the form and use the verified charity
choice.subtitle: Return to the independently located Cedar Valley Community Recovery Alliance record.

feedback.heading: The unverified form receives nothing

choice.title: Enter card details, then cancel

feedback.heading: Canceling helps, but entered card details may be exposed

artifact.heading: The charity uses the entered phone number

artifact.transcript: An unexpected simulated call comes from fictional Morgan Reed, Donation Response Coordinator for National Relief Support Fund. Morgan says, "Every minute you wait, families suffer." Morgan claims charity databases are slow after disasters, the organization is too new to appear everywhere, and the learner already started a pledge. Morgan offers to preserve the matching funds with a smaller payment. The call demonstrates how contact information entered without payment can enable targeted pressure.

scene.question: How would you respond to the follow-up call?
scene.description: It is never too late to stop. Recovery should match the contact information already exposed.

warningSigns.sign: The caller used information from the abandoned form.
Guilt and urgency replace answers to verification concerns.
A smaller payment is presented as a safe compromise.

choice.title: End the call and address the information exposure
choice.subtitle: Block and report the contact, preserve evidence, review privacy settings, and expect follow-up scams.

feedback.heading: You stopped the pressure and matched recovery to the exposure
feedback.consequence: No card information or money is sent, and the exposed contact details receive attention.
feedback.explanation: Targeted follow-up messages may mention charities, disasters, banking, or identity concerns.

warningSigns.sign: The unexpected call proves the entered details are already being used.

choice.title: Say you donate only through independently chosen organizations
choice.subtitle: End the call, block future contacts, and preserve the form and caller details.

feedback.heading: A clear giving boundary ends the call
feedback.consequence: No payment follows the contact-information exposure.
feedback.explanation: Legitimate giving does not require obeying a stranger's deadline.

warningSigns.sign: The caller treated verification as harmful to victims.

choice.title: Ask for an employee ID and callback number
choice.subtitle: Continue the conversation using details supplied by Morgan.

feedback.heading: Caller-supplied details are not independent proof
feedback.consequence: Morgan provides a convincing ID and a number controlled by the same unverified organization.
feedback.explanation: A badge, employee ID, pledge number, case number, or callback can be invented.

warningSigns.sign: The person being checked also controls the verification route.

choice.title: Stay on the line while researching

feedback.heading: The search is independent, but the pressure is not paused
feedback.consequence: The exact charity still fails verification, although Morgan keeps trying to reinterpret the results.

warningSigns.sign: Morgan asks to remain part of the verification process.

choice.title: Continue to payment under guilt

feedback.heading: Guilt moves the conversation toward payment

warningSigns.sign: The phrase about families suffering is used to shorten decision time.

artifact.heading: Simulated, nonfunctional payment selection

artifact.transcript: A clearly simulated and nonfunctional payment page offers direct card entry, a fictional person-to-person payment to Morgan Reed, wire transfer, cryptocurrency, gift cards, or a check mailed to an incomplete processing-center address. The recipient name Morgan Reed does not match National Relief Support Fund. The page claims unusual methods release matching funds faster. It includes no real brands, accounts, handles, wallet addresses, QR codes, or operational payment instructions.

scene.question: Which response is safest at the payment-method screen?

warningSigns.sign: The payment-app recipient is a person rather than the charity.
